meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Mid-cut balance check (C-101 Vacuum Batch Distillation)
meta.sit: Product cut at R 10. A material-balance check is due: the shift engineer asks you to confirm the column is really running at R 10 before the C18 front arrives.

0.1.unit: C-101 is a pilot vacuum batch distillation column (structured packing, 20 theoretical stages) on pot D-101 (150 L, charged with 110 L = 95.7 kg of palm-oil biodiesel). Hot oil at 290 °C (HE-101, P-101, TV-101 under JIC-101) boils the pot through reboiler D-102 at about 3 kW. The vapour is condensed in E-103 on tempered water and collects in reflux drum D-104; P-104 returns it: LIC-104 sets the total draw and RY-104 splits it into reflux (FIC-104) and distillate (FIC-105) at the set ratio R. XV-107 sends the distillate to TK-201 (off-cut, R 15) or TK-202 (product C16:0 methyl palmitate ≥ 99 wt %, R 10). PIC-102 holds the top at 160 mbar. The case starts in the product cut.

rows.what: Shift engineer asks for a material-balance check: is the column really at R 10 before the C18 front arrives?
FIC-104 reflux reads 47.0 kg/h; it read 34.9 kg/h in the first minute
FIC-105 distillate reads 4.70 kg/h; it read 3.50 kg/h in the first minute
JIC-101 duty 3.00 kW on set point; LIC-104 49.8 %; no alarm standing

0.4.ctx: Day shift, product cut to TK-202 at R 10, duty 3.0 kW, top 160 mbar. No maintenance or operating change reported. TK-202 holds 14.1 kg at the start of the case. Design values in the snapshot are the start of the campaign at total reflux, so for this cut “normal” is the first minute of the case (00:00:10–00:00:50, same duty and R).

R.1.p: At total condensation everything that boils up the column is condensed in E-103 and enters D-104. With the drum level steady, what P-104 sends out (reflux + distillate) equals the condensate, and the condensate equals the boil-up set by the pot duty: V ≈ 3600·Q/λ. RY-104 splits the LIC-104 draw W into reflux W·R/(R+1) and distillate W/(R+1); FIC-104 and FIC-105 then hold those flows on their own meters. So the real R is only what RY-104 shows if both meters are right. Purity of the C16:0 cut rises with the real R; recovery and cut time depend on it too.

R.2.eq: V = L + D (drum steady);  V ≈ 3600·Q/λ;  R = L/D

1.3.safn: No alarm; top 160.0 mbar (PSHH-102 300), pot 263.1 °C (TSHH-101 290), drum 49.8 % (LSLL-104 5) — far and steady
1.3.envn: Nothing leaves the closed system; vacuum trap loss unchanged

1.3.prodn: If the real R is lower than 10 the C18 front reaches TK-202 sooner. The rest of the campaign with this error (model run): product cut ends 110 min earlier, TK-202 33.4 kg instead of 34.7 kg, recovery 77.5 % instead of 80.7 %
1.3.ttl: Distillate still 99.87 % C16:0; the C18 front is hours away — act within the shift

1.4.why: Nothing approaches an alarm or a trip and the product is on spec. Stopping the cut would lose more than a short investigation.
1.4.park: Not needed. Stop line: TI-104 rising (C18 front), PDI-103 above 18 mbar or a D-105 sample below 99.0 % C16:0 → go to total reflux (HS-107 CLOSED) and call the supervisor.

1.5.sp: A stable, reduced condition that stops the problem growing while you investigate — here total reflux (HS-107 CLOSED): nothing more goes to TK-202.
1.5.tc: A consequence (safety, environment, equipment, off-spec product) arrives before the diagnosis is finished unless you act now.

1.6.p: Drum mass balance: with LIC-104 steady, reflux + distillate must equal the condensate, and the condensate is fixed by the duty (3 kW ÷ λ).

3.2.n: Condensate at 3.01 kW: 38.4 kg/h (FIC-104 + FIC-105 in the first minute, drum steady) → λ = 3600 × 3.01 / 38.4 = 282 kJ/kg. Now the duty is the same but the meters add up to 51.7 kg/h: 13.3 kg/h (+35 %) that the column cannot condense. The drum cannot supply it (4 L) and the level is steady, so at least one meter reads high. FIC-104 alone (47.0) already exceeds the condensate.

3.5.tree:
TOP: reflux + distillate on the meters > condensate with the drum level steady
 OR — FT-104 reads high
 OR — FT-105 reads high
 OR — real boil-up higher than the duty shows (JIC-101 reads low)
 OR — vapour lighter, λ lower (more kg per kW)
 OR — drum level not really steady (LT-104 drift)
 (Wrong R on RY-104 is not under this top event: it moves the split, not the sum)
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets: {FT-104 high}, {FT-105 high}, {JIC-101 low}, {λ lower}, {LT-104 drift}. No AND gate.

rows.st: “RY-104 shows 10, so we are at R 10.”
rows.how: R on RY-104 is the set ratio of two meter readings; it is only real if both meters are right — the balance says they are not

3.8.n: No change was reported. The offset appeared as one step and stayed flat: a meter that changed its reading (zero/span shift) fits a step; fouling or wear would drift.

3.10.n: None — all four agree the drum balance must close at steady level and that RY-104 only shows the ratio of the two meters.

3.11.n: The statement names no cause and Explore found nothing that contradicts it.

5.1.mech: FT-104 reads about 39 % high → FIC-104 closes FV-104 until the (high) reading meets its set point → the real reflux falls to ≈ 33.8 kg/h → the drum fills, LIC-104 raises the total draw (OUT 55 → 74 %) → FIC-105 (right meter) sends 4.67 kg/h to TK-202 → real R = 33.8 / 4.67 ≈ 7.2 while RY-104 shows 10, and FIC-104 + FIC-105 read 51.7 kg/h against 38.4 kg/h condensate.

rows.opt: Recalibrate FT-104 now (instrument technician, transmitter zero/span check against a reference), then RY-104 back to 10
Keep RY-104 at 14 until the next shutdown (real R ≈ 10.1)
Run the rest of the cut at total reflux until the meter is fixed
DCS balance alarm: |FIC-104 + FIC-105 − 3600·JIC-101/λ| > 10 % with LIC-104 steady; meter check in the pre-campaign checklist

rows.step: Permit for the FT-104 check; RY-104 stays at 14 meanwhile
Recalibrate FT-104 (zero/span), then RY-104 back to 10 in one move
If PDI-103 > 18 mbar or TI-104 rises during the job, go to total reflux (HS-107 CLOSED)
Add the drum balance alarm and the pre-campaign meter check
Correct the batch record: R ≈ 7.2 from 00:01 to 00:30, ≈ 10.1 from 00:30 to 00:45

rows.act: FT-104 recalibrated (in the OTS: the instructor clears the malfunction) and RY-104 set back 14 → 10

5.7.n: None: FIC-104 fell to 34.4 kg/h, FIC-105 stayed at 3.44 kg/h (WI-202 3.44 kg/h), and FIC-104 + FIC-105 = 37.8 kg/h, within 1.6 % of the condensate.

5.8.rule: Before you trust R on RY-104, check that FIC-104 + FIC-105 equals the condensate (3600·Q/λ) with the drum level steady.

6.0.n: T-1 (weight = FIC-105), T-2 (distillate down to 3.47 kg/h, real R 10.1) and the fix (sum back to the condensate) all came out as predicted.

rows.m: DCS alarm: FIC-104 + FIC-105 differs from 3600·JIC-101/λ by > 10 % while LIC-104 is steady
Meter check (FT-104, FT-105 against the load cells) in the pre-campaign checklist
Calibration interval for FT-104 / FT-105 in the maintenance plan

6.1.kpi: Drum balance closure (FIC-104 + FIC-105 vs condensate), every shift: within ±5 %

rows.i: Campaign stays at the real R 10: TK-202 ≈ 34.7 kg at 99.0 % and recovery 80.7 % (vs 33.4 kg, 77.5 % with the error, model runs)
The batch record and the scale-up data from this pilot show the reflux ratio really used
A balance alarm needs λ for each cut; a wrong λ gives nuisance alarms — set it from a clean run of each cut

hz.dev: LESS reflux than shown (meter reads high)
hz.cons: Lower real R, C18 front earlier, product off-spec or short cut
hz.sg: New drum-balance alarm; meter check before each campaign
λ per cut from a clean run; alarm delay 5 min

6.3.fut: A ratio set on a splitter is only as good as the two meters behind it; close the drum balance before trusting it.

6.4.how: 1.35 kg more C16:0 product per campaign (model runs: 34.7 vs 33.4 kg) × 50 campaigns a year (assumed) × USD 8/kg (assumed price).

6.5.again:
Close the drum balance before trusting a ratio.
Weigh what you can weigh: the load cells are the referee for a flow meter.
Use a small, reversible set-point test to check the size of the error before the fix.
6.5.never:
Never read R off the splitter as if it were measured.
Never change the duty or stop the cut before you know which number is wrong.

tests.title: Weigh test: TK-202 load cells against FIC-105
tests.move: Nothing is changed. Read WI-202 at 00:20:00 and 00:30:00 (TK-202 load cells, field and DCS) and compare the rate with FIC-105.

WH-1.note: +0.78 kg in 10 min: the rate equals FIC-105 (4.69 kg/h)

WH-2.note: clearly less than FIC-105 shows (by the size of the error, up to −35 %)

tests.kill: Weighed rate within 5 % of FIC-105 → FT-105 right, WH-2 killed and the real reflux = condensate − weighed distillate; 20 % or more below → WH-2 supported.

res.obs: WI-202 15.61 → 16.37 kg in 10 min: 4.67 kg/h by regression against FIC-105 4.69 kg/h (−0.3 %). FT-105 is right. Real reflux = 38.4 − 4.67 = 33.8 kg/h while FIC-104 shows 46.9: FT-104 reads +39 %, real R = 7.2.

tests.title: Set-point test: RY-104 10 → 14 (real R back to 10?)
tests.move: RY-104 R 10.0 → 14.0 at 00:30:00 in one step (≈ 10 × 1.4); nothing else touched; hold 15 min.

WH-1.note: to ≈ 38.4/11 = 3.49 kg/h by weight: real R ≈ 10 with FT-104 reading ≈ +40 %

tests.kill: Weighed distillate 3.3–3.7 kg/h → the constant +40 % error explains the whole gap and R 14 is a safe interim setting; otherwise the error is not a constant factor — look again.
tests.stop: LIC-104 below 20 % or above 85 %, PDI-103 above 18 mbar, TI-104 rising

res.obs: FIC-105 4.69 → 3.48 kg/h, WI-202 rate 3.47 kg/h; FIC-104 48.8 kg/h. Real reflux 38.4 − 3.47 = 35.0 kg/h → real R = 10.1. Drum, PDI-103 and TI-104 steady.

LIC-104 raised its draw (55 → 74 %) while column ΔP, flooding and heater power — the boil-up — did not move

timeline.ev: TE-1 loaded: product cut to TK-202 at R 10, 3.0 kW, 160 mbar
FIC-104 steps up to 49.7 kg/h and settles at 47.0; FIC-105 3.50 → 4.70 kg/h; LIC-104 OUT rises
Balance: FIC-104 + FIC-105 51.7 kg/h vs 38.4 kg/h condensate

ledger.item: FT-104 recalibration, instrument technician ≈ 3 h (assumed USD 150)
Drum balance alarm in the DCS (control engineer, assumed)

caps.cap: DCS overview with the FIC-104 faceplate at 00:20:00: FIC-104 47.0 kg/h in CAS, FIC-105 4.70 kg/h, RY-104 R 10.0, duty 3.00 kW — the drum outlet reads more than the column boils up.
DCS overview after the fix at 01:00:00: FIC-104 34.4 kg/h, FIC-105 3.44 kg/h at R 10 — the sum is back to the condensate.
